description: In less than eight months, Russia went from the rule of the tsars to the rule of the Bolsheviks. 1917 invented a model that would divide the world for decades.

hero.hook: In eight months, a thousand-year-old empire fell, and the 20th century split in two.

blocks.text: In **1917**, in less than eight months, Russia moved from absolute monarchy to a state run by the **Bolsheviks**, a revolutionary party led by **Vladimir Lenin**. This was not a simple uprising. It was the collapse of an empire under the weight of war, and then the seizure of the empty space it left.
That shift created a model that would divide the world for much of the 20th century.

In the [[First World War]] since 1914, Russia could no longer keep up. Already **1.7 million** soldiers dead. Mutinies. Shortages of flour and coal in **Petrograd**, the capital, today Saint Petersburg. Tsar **Nicholas II** refused the reforms demanded by the [[Douma]], the Russian parliament.

blocks.caption: Nicholas II, the last tsar of an exhausted monarchy

blocks.text: The poison meant to kill [[Rasputin]], a monk with great influence at court, was supposedly neutralized by the sugar in the cakes it was hidden in. The legend of his murder says a lot about how far the throne had sunk.

By taking personal command at the front in **1915**, the tsar became the only man to blame for every defeat. Rasputin's hold over the tsarina **Alexandra** finished off what was left of the imperial family's prestige.

In **February 1917**, by the [[Julian calendar]] then used in Russia and running several days behind the West, the revolution started over bread. Women workers marched into the streets. The city garrison joined them. Nicholas II abdicated on **March 2**, ending **300 years** of Romanov rule.

blocks.caption: Petrograd 1917: the street takes over from the throne

blocks.text: What followed was a “dual power.” On one side, a legal **Provisional Government**. On the other, the [[Petrograd Soviet]], a council of workers and soldiers that controlled the factories and the barracks. **Alexander Kerensky**, the face of the Provisional Government, kept Russia in the war. The people wanted peace, bread, and land.

sections.title: February: the end of the Romanovs

blocks.text: Lenin came back from exile in a “sealed train” arranged by Germany, which hoped to weaken Russia. In April his [[April Theses]] landed like a slap: **“Peace, Bread, Land.”** With [[Leon Trotsky]], an organizer without equal, the Bolsheviks prepared the insurrection.

blocks.caption: Lenin, the strategist of a carefully organized seizure of power

blocks.text: When the Winter Palace was taken, the tsars' wine cellars were so vast that guards had to be posted to keep the revolution from drinking itself into a stupor.

On the night of **November 7, 1917** (October 25 by the Russian calendar), the bridges, stations, and telegraph offices fell almost without a shot. The Winter Palace, seat of the Provisional Government, followed. A bloody civil war then ran until **1922**.

The **Cheka**, the Bolshevik political police, launched the terror. In July **1918**, the imperial family was executed at Yekaterinburg. The peace of [[Brest-Litovsk]] pulled Russia out of the war at the cost of heavy territorial losses. In **1922** came the **USSR**, the first state built on [[Marxism-Leninism]], the ideology that joins Marx's ideas to Lenin's methods.

blocks.text: In **1917**, the collapse of tsarism and the Bolshevik seizure of power turned a protest over bread into the birth of the world's first communist state.
